arxiv-1903-07525.title: PZnet: Efficient 3D ConvNet Inference on Manycore CPUs
arxiv-1903-07525.creator: Sergiy Popovych 1, Davit Buniatyan 1, Aleksandar Zlateski 2, Kai Li 1, H. Sebastian Seung 1
arxiv-1903-07525.description: Abstract Convolutional nets have been shown to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in many biomedical image analysis tasks. Many tasks within biomedical analysis domain involve analyzing volumetric (3D) data acquired by CT, MRI and Microscopy acquisition methods. To deploy convolutional nets in practical working systems, it is important to solve the efficient inference problem.

arxiv-2107-05171.title: Shadow and near-horizon characteristics of the acoustic charged black hole in curved spacetime
arxiv-2107-05171.creator: Ru Ling, Hong Guo, Hang Liu, Xiao-Mei Kuang, Bin Wang
arxiv-2107-05171.description: Abstract In this paper, we first analyze the horizon structure of the acoustic charged black hole in curved spacetime, and then study its acoustic shadow as well as the near-horizon characteristics including the quasinormal modes (QNM) frequencies and analogue Hawking radiation.

arxiv-2205-00829.title: Function Decomposition Tree with Causality-First Perspective and Systematic Description of Problems in Materials Informatics
arxiv-2205-00829.creator: Hiori Kino, Hieu-Chi Dam, Takashi Miyake, Riichiro Mizoguchi
arxiv-2205-00829.description: Abstract As interdisciplinary science is flourishing because of materials informatics and additional factors; a systematic way is required for expressing knowledge and facilitating communication between scientists in various fields. A function decomposition tree is such a representation, but domain scientists face difficulty in constructing it.

arxiv-2212-09422.title: Human in the loop: How to effectively create coherent topics by manually labeling only a few documents per class
arxiv-2212-09422.creator: Anton Thielmann, Benjamin Säfken, Christoph Weisser
arxiv-2212-09422.description: Abstract Few-shot methods for accurate modeling under sparse label-settings have improved significantly. However, the applications of few-shot modeling in natural language processing remain solely in the field of document classification. With recent performance improvements, supervised few-shot methods, combined with a simple topic extraction method pose a significant challenge to unsupervised topic modeling methods.

arxiv-2311-10080.title: Asymptotics of approximate Bayesian computation when summary statistics converge at heterogeneous rates
arxiv-2311-10080.creator: Caroline Lawless, Christian P. Robert, Judith Rousseau, Robin J. Ryder
arxiv-2311-10080.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Likelihood-free methods in Bayesian statistics are methods for posterior inference in situations where likelihoods are intractable or unavailable in closed form, but may be simulated from. Such situations are typical of real-life applications, when models are defined by complex generative processes.

arxiv-2311-14905.title: Class Gradient Projection For Continual Learning Conference: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 10–14, 2022; Lisboa, Portugal. Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’22), Oct. 10–14, 2022, Lisboa, Portugal Price: 15.00 ISBN: 9
arxiv-2311-14905.creator: Cheng Chen, Ji Zhang, Jingkuan Song 1,2, Lianli Gao
arxiv-2311-14905.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cheng Chen, Ji Zhang, Jingkuan Song 1,2, Lianli Gao. Catastrophic forgetting is one of the most critical challenges in Continual Learning (CL). Recent approaches tackle this problem by projecting the gradient update orthogonal to the gradient subspace of existing tasks. While the results are remarkable, those approaches ignore the fact that these calculated gradients are not guaranteed to be orthogonal to the gradient subspace of each class due to the class deviation in tasks, e.g., distinguishing “Man” from “Sea” v.s. differentiating “Boy” from “Girl”.

arxiv-2312-13536.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptive Graph Classification
arxiv-2312-13536.creator: Siyang Luo, Ziyi Jiang, Zhenghan Chen \sthanks Contact author: 1979282882@pku.edu.cn, Xiaoxuan Liang
arxiv-2312-13536.description: Abstract Despite the remarkable accomplishments of graph neural networks (GNNs), they typically rely on task-specific labels, posing potential challenges in terms of their acquisition. Existing work have been made to address this issue through the lens of unsupervised domain adaptation, wherein labeled source graphs are utilized to enhance the learning process for target data.

arxiv-2403-10536.title: Interaction between U-shaped amyloid beta fibril and semiconducting silicon nitride monolayer
arxiv-2403-10536.creator: Ashkan Shekaari, Mahmoud Jafari
arxiv-2403-10536.description: Abstract Motivated by some recent works showing the ability of semiconducting monolayers to disintegrate the structures of biological fibrils, we have applied molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in both classical and quantum regimes to investigate whether semiconducting Si 3 N 4 monolayer has the same ability on interaction with U-shaped amyloid beta (A β \beta ) fibril.

arxiv-2407-07947.title: Minimum-entropy constraints on galactic potentials
arxiv-2407-07947.creator: Leandro Beraldo e Silva, Monica Valluri, Eugene Vasiliev, Kohei Hattori, Walter de Siqueira Pedra, Kathryne J. Daniel
arxiv-2407-07947.description: Abstract A tracer sample in a gravitational potential, starting from a generic initial condition, phase-mixes towards a stationary state. This evolution is accompanied by an entropy increase, and the final state is characterized by a distribution function (DF) that depends only on integrals of motion (Jeans’ theorem).

arxiv-2508-00557.title: Training-Free Class Purification for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2508-00557.creator: Qi Chen, Lingxiao Yang, Yun Chen, Nailong Zhao, Jianhuang Lai, Jie Shao, Xiaohua Xie
arxiv-2508-00557.description: Abstract Fine-tuning pre-trained vision-language models has emerged as a powerful approach for enhancing open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS). However, the substantial computational and resource demands associated with training on large datasets have prompted interest in training-free methods for OVSS. Existing training-free approaches primarily focus on modifying model architectures and generating prototypes to improve segmentation performance.

pmc-10741877.title: GABAA Receptor Benzodiazepine Binding Sites and Motor Impairments in Parkinson’s Disease
pmc-10741877.creator: Nicolaas I. Bohnen, Jaimie Barr, Robert Vangel, Stiven Roytman, Rebecca Paalanen, Kirk A. Frey, Peter J. H. Scott, Prabesh Kanel
pmc-10741877.description: Flumazenil is an allosteric modulator of the γ-aminobutyric acid-A receptor (GABAAR) benzodiazepine binding site that could normalize neuronal signaling and improve motor impairments in Parkinson’s disease (PD). Little is known about how regional GABAAR availability affects motor symptoms. We investigated the relationship between regional availability of GABAAR benzodiazepine binding sites and motor impairments in PD.

pmc-11291294.title: Solving a diagnostic dilemma in a patient with periodic fever—When the pieces of the puzzle finally fit
pmc-11291294.creator: Vanita Shukla, Virendra R. S. Sarabjit Singh, Cara Ranghell, Celine Ramgoolam, Nicole S. Solomon, Vidya Ramcharitar‐Maharaj, Christophe Persad, Keisha Davis‐King
pmc-11291294.description: Key Clinical MessageThe lack of pediatric subspecialists locally prior to 5 years ago, meant that some of our patients with rare, relapsing conditions were left behind. Familial Mediterranean fever can be diagnosed clinically and supported via genetic panel studies. Although neurological symptoms can be non‐specific, this system symptomatology may lead patients and carers to seek medical attention.

pmc-11347834.title: Artificial intelligence-driven reverse vaccinology for Neisseria gonorrhoeae vaccine: Prioritizing epitope-based candidates
pmc-11347834.creator: Ravi Kant, Mohd. Shoaib Khan, Madhu Chopra, Daman Saluja
pmc-11347834.description: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the causative agent of the sexually transmitted disease gonorrhea. The increasing prevalence of this disease worldwide, the rise of antibiotic-resistant strains, and the difficulties in treatment necessitate the development of a vaccine, highlighting the significance of preventative measures to control and eradicate the infection.

pmc-11713000.title: Integrating Pilot Study Findings into Larger Intervention Trials for Dementia Advance Care Planning
pmc-11713000.creator: Kara B Dassel, Jordana L Clayton, Eli Iacob, Rebecca Utz, Sara Bybee, Katherine P Supiano, Nancy R Aruscavage
pmc-11713000.description: BackgroundPersons with dementia often lose decisional capacity before death, underscoring the need for dementia‐focused advance care planning tools. We created LEAD (Life‐Planning in Early Alzheimer’s and Other Dementias). This intervention guides patients with early‐stage dementia and their care partners through conversations to identify and discuss the patient’s values and preferences for end‐of‐life care.

pmc-12608817.title: Multi-Analytical Assessment of Deterioration in the Qianlong Tripitaka Wooden Scripture Plates
pmc-12608817.creator: Wangting Wu, Yuhan Peng, Jianrui Zha, Ge Zhang, Mengdie Lv, Yingzhu Wang, Luis Alves
pmc-12608817.description: The Qianlong Tripitaka preserved in the Capital Museum is a distinctive large-scale wood block printing plates of the Qing Dynasty. It represents a unique type of Chinese documentary wooden heritage preserved in a dry museum environment, which has rarely been subjected to comprehensive physicochemical analysis, resulting in an inadequate understanding of their deterioration processes.

pmc-12690074.title: Temperature field ultrafast detection and identification quantum sensor based on diamond array
pmc-12690074.creator: Wei Gao, Jinyu Tai, Zhiqiang Xiang, Yunbo Shi, Xin Li, Huanfei Wen, Fei Deng, Zhonghao Li, Zongmin Ma, Hailong Wang, Weixuan Zhang, Zheng Lou, Hao Guo, Jun Tang, Lili Wang, Jun Liu
pmc-12690074.description: Ultrafast temperature field detection and identification is crucial for applications ranging from environmental sensing and biomedical monitoring to thermal management in advanced energy systems. Conventional temperature sensors—comprising discrete sensing arrays, data storage units, and external processors—suffer from high latency due to slow sensor response, repeated analog-to-digital conversions, and extensive data transmission inherent to von Neumann architectures.

pmc-12787860.title: Automated Neuromuscular Assessment: Machine-Learning-Based Facial Palsy Classification Using Surface Electromyography
pmc-12787860.creator: Ibrahim Manzoor, Aryana Popescu, Sarah Ricchizzi, Aldo Spolaore, Mykola Gorbachuk, Marcos Tatagiba, Georgios Naros, Kathrin Machetanz
pmc-12787860.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Time-domain EMG features during facial movements effectively reflect facial nerve dysfunction.Ensemble ML models achieved up to ~84.8% accuracy in automated HB classification from EMG data in facial palsy. What are the implications of the main findings? EMG-based ML enables objective, non-invasive assessment of facial palsy severity.

pmc-13122710.title: Generic health literacy of adults in Germany. Results of the Panel ‘Health in Germany’ 2024
pmc-13122710.creator: Susanne Jordan, Simon Löbl
pmc-13122710.description: BackgroundGeneric health literacy (HL) encompasses cross-thematic and cross-contextual skills, motivation and knowledge in dealing with health information. Low HL is associated with higher healthcare needs and unfavourable health behaviours.MethodData from the RKI Panel 2024 (n = 26,817) will be used to provide a current overview of HL among adults. HL was measured using the HLS19-Q12.

pmc-13232624.title: Brain and knee joint degeneration following anterior cruciate ligament injury in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13232624.creator: Wei Yao, Barton L Wise, Yu-Yang Lin, Ming Fan, Shanxiu Xu, I-Shin Ju, Jonathan I Berg, Jill L Silverman, Gabriela G Loots, Blaine A Christiansen
pmc-13232624.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and osteoarthritis (OA) are 2 of the most common health conditions affecting the elderly. Recent studies in mice and humans have described an association between OA and AD, with prevalent OA increasing the risk of developing AD-like cognitive declines.
